subject: Spanska
title: Greetings and school phrases
sourceSummary: Basic greetings, polite phrases, and words for the classroom and school life.

questions.prompt: How do you say "Hi, my name is Elena" in Spanish?
questions.opener: The verb llamarse is used to say what your name is.
questions.explanation: "Me llamo" means "my name is" (literally "I call myself"). "Tú te llamas" is "your name is", and "adiós" means "goodbye", not "hi".

questions.opener: A common, casual greeting between friends.
questions.explanation: "¿Qué tal?" is a casual way of asking "how are you?" or "what's up?", similar to "¿Cómo estás?".

questions.prompt: Someone says "Gracias". What do you politely reply?
questions.opener: What do you say in Spanish when you receive a thank you?
questions.explanation: "De nada" means "you're welcome"/"no problem" and is the usual reply to a thank you. "Por favor" means "please", and "lo siento" means "I'm sorry".

questions.prompt: What does "¿Puedo ir al baño?" mean?
questions.opener: A question you often need to ask during a lesson.
choices: May I go to the bathroom?
questions.explanation: "¿Puedo...?" means "may I...?" and "el baño" is the bathroom. The whole phrase means "May I go to the bathroom?".

questions.prompt: The teacher says "Abrid el libro, por favor". What should you do?
questions.explanation: "Abrir" means "to open", so "abrid el libro" means "open the book". "Por favor" means "please".

questions.prompt: Write a Spanish word that means "good night".
questions.opener: You say it when you're going to bed.

questions.prompt: Correct the two errors: "Hola! Como te llamas? Yo me llama Marc."
questions.opener: Check the question word and the verb form for "I".
questions.answer: ¡Hola! ¿Cómo te llamas? Yo me llamo Marc.
steps: Questions in Spanish open with an upside-down question mark: "¿Cómo te llamas?", not just "Como te llamas?".
"Yo me llama" → "Yo me llamo". The verb llamarse conjugates for "I" (yo) as "llamo", not "llama" (which is for he/she).
The same applies to exclamation marks: "¡Hola!" should have an upside-down exclamation mark before it.

questions.prompt: Which greetings and polite phrases should you know at the grade 7 level in Spanish?
questions.opener: The most common phrases for greeting, thanking, and asking for help.
questions.answer: Greetings: Hola = hi · Buenos días = good morning · Buenas tardes = good afternoon · Buenas noches = good night/good evening · Adiós = goodbye · Hasta luego = see you later. How are you: ¿Qué tal? / ¿Cómo estás? = how are you? · Bien, gracias = good, thanks. Politeness: Por favor = please · Gracias = thank you · De nada = you're welcome · Lo siento = I'm sorry · Perdón = excuse me. School: ¿Puedo...? = may I...? · el baño = the bathroom · abrir/cerrar el libro = open/close the book.
